supervision.d: The act or instance of supervising.
supervision.e: Under his parents' supervision he drilled the holes in the wood.

supplement.d: Something added, especially to make up for a deficiency.

suppress.d: To put an end to, especially with force, to crush, do away with; to prohibit, subdue.
suppress.e: I struggled to suppress my smile.

surge.d: A sudden transient rush, flood or increase.
surge.e: He felt a surge of excitement.

suspicious.e: His suspicious behaviour brought him to the attention of the police.

swift.d: A small plain-colored bird of the family Apodidae that resembles a swallow and is noted for its rapid flight.

sympathetic.d: Of, related to, showing, or characterized by sympathy
sympathetic.e: John looked very upset. I gave him a sympathetic look.

tail.d: The caudal appendage of an animal that is attached to its posterior and near the anus.
tail.e: Most primates have a tail and fangs.

technically.e: Technically he was Canadian, but everyone assumed he was American.

temporarily.d: For a limited period of time; not permanently.

terrifying.d: To frighten greatly; to fill with terror.

territory.d: A large extent or tract of land; for example a region, country or district.

theme.d: A subject of a talk or an artistic piece; a topic.
theme.e: We themed the birthday party around superheroes.

therapy.d: Attempted remediation of a health problem following a diagnosis, usually synonymous with treatment.

thoroughly.d: In a thorough or complete manner.
thoroughly.e: He went out in the rain and came back thoroughly drenched.

thread.d: A cord formed by spinning or twisting together textile fibers or filaments into one or more continuous strands, typically used in needlework.

threaten.d: To make a threat against someone; to use threats.
threaten.e: He threatened me with a knife.

thrill.d: A trembling or quivering, especially one caused by emotion.

throat.d: The front part of the neck.
throat.e: The wild pitch bounced and hit the catcher in the throat.

tiresome.e: Eventually his long stories became tiresome.

toenail.d: The thin, horny, transparent plate covering the upper surface of the end of a toe.

toil.d: Labour, work, especially of a grueling nature.

tolerant.d: Tending to permit, allow, understand, or accept something
tolerant.e: He's pretty tolerant of different political views, but don't ask him about religion.

tolerate.d: To allow or permit without explicit approval, usually if it is perceived as negative.
tolerate.e: I can tolerate working on Saturday, but not Sunday.

toll.d: Loss or damage incurred through a disaster.
toll.e: The war has taken its toll on the people.

tomb.d: A small building, or a room within one, for the remains of the dead, with walls, a roof, and (if it is to be used for more than one corpse) a door. It may be partly or wholly in the ground (except for its entrance) in a cemetery, or it may be inside a church proper or in its crypt. Single tombs may be permanently sealed; those for families (or other groups) have doors for access whenever needed.

ton.d: Any of various units of mass, originally notionally equal to the contents of a tun, particularly: The short ton of 2000 pounds (about 907 kg), 20 hundredweights of 100 pounds avoirdupois each. The long ton of 2240 pounds (about 1016 kg), 20 hundredweights of 112 pounds avoirdupois each. The metric ton of 1000 kilograms (about 2205 lb), 10 quintals of 100 kilograms each.

torch.d: A stick of wood or plant fibres twisted together, with one end soaked in a flammable substance such as resin or tallow and set on fire, which is held in the hand, put into a wall bracket, or stuck into the ground, and used chiefly as a light source.
torch.e: The mob of angry villagers carried torches and pitchforks to the vampire’s castle.

tough.d: A person who obtains things by force; a thug or bully.
tough.e: The tent, made of tough canvas, held up to many abuses.

toxic.d: Having a chemical nature that is harmful to health or lethal if consumed or otherwise entering into the body in sufficient quantities.
toxic.e: Tobacco smoke contains many toxic substances.

trait.d: An identifying characteristic, habit or trend.
trait.e: The number one personality trait I hate is hypocrisy. Why can't you be consistent!?

transfusion.d: The transfer of blood or blood products from one individual to another.

translator.d: A person who translates text, film or other material into a different natural language.

tray.d: A small, typically rectangular or round, flat, and rigid object upon which things are carried.
tray.e: I carefully arranged the dishes on the tray and brought it upstairs.

tricky.e: They were in a tricky situation.

trivial.d: Any of the three liberal arts forming the trivium.

troop.d: (collective) A collection of people; a number; a multitude (in general).

tub.d: A flat-bottomed vessel, of width similar to or greater than its height, used for storing or packing things, or for washing things in.
tub.e: He bought a tub of lard to roast the potatoes in.

tuberculosis.d: An infectious disease of humans and animals caused by a species of mycobacterium, usually Mycobacterium tuberculosis, mainly infecting the lungs where it causes tubercles characterized by the expectoration of mucus and sputum, fever, weight loss, and chest pain, and transmitted through inhalation or ingestion of bacteria.

tuition.d: A sum of money paid for instruction (such as in a high school, boarding school, university, or college).
tuition.e: These rosemaling workshops are no place for anyone who wants to pester me or the students with the "white privilege" card, inter alia. Therefore, I reserve the right to refund the tuition of such men and women, kick them out the door, and bar them from at least two of my future events.

tumor.d: An abnormal growth; differential diagnosis includes abscess, metaplasia, and neoplasia.

ultimate.d: The most basic or fundamental of a set of things

s: at the end of the day
when all is said and done

unavailable.d: (history) A communist who operated underground and was therefore not available for a political leadership position.
unavailable.e: A cold, reserved man, he was seen as emotionally unavailable.

unbearable.d: So unpleasant or painful as to be unendurable

unbeatable.d: That cannot be beaten, defeated or overcome

unchanged.d: Not changed or altered; remaining in an original state.

uncommon.d: Rare; not readily found; unusual. (clarification of this definition is needed (uncommon > rare > very uncommon))
uncommon.e: Bald eagles are an uncommon sighting in this state.

unconcerned.d: Indifferent and having no interest; aloof.
unconcerned.e: She is completely unconcerned about the upcoming exams.

unconscious.e: After the anesthetist administered the general anesthetic the patient was unconscious.

underestimate.d: An estimate that is too low.

undergraduate.d: A student at a university who has not yet received a degree.
undergraduate.e: After completing my undergraduate studies, I embarked on a career in publishing.

underground.d: Below the ground; below the surface of the Earth.
underground.e: There is an underground tunnel that takes you across the river.

undersea.d: Existing, relating to, or made for use beneath the sea, that is, beneath the sea surface, inside the sea.

understanding.d: The act of one that understands or comprehends; the mental process of discernment of meaning.
understanding.e: There are certain things that defy human understanding.

undertake.d: To take upon oneself; to start, to embark on (a specific task etc.).
undertake.e: He undertook to exercise more in future.

underwear.d: Clothes worn next to the skin, underneath outer clothing.

unforeseen.d: An event, incident, cost, etc. that was not foreseen.

utility.d: The state or condition of being useful; usefulness.

utilize.d: To make use of; to use.

utterly.d: Completely, entirely, to the fullest extent

valid.e: I will believe him as soon as he offers a valid answer.

vanity.d: That which is vain, futile, or worthless; that which is of no value, use or profit.

varied.e: He varies his magic tricks so as to minimize the possibility that any given audience member will see the same trick twice.

version.d: A specific form or variation of something.
version.e: It's only in the King James Version of the Bible.

versus.e: It is the Packers versus the Steelers in the Super Bowl.

viewer.d: Someone who views a spectacle; an onlooker or spectator.

vigorously.d: With intense energy, force or vigor
vigorously.e: He knocked vigorously on the door.

vigour.d: Active strength or force of body or mind; a capacity for exertion, physically, intellectually, or morally; energy.

villa.d: A house, often larger and more expensive than average, in the countryside or on the coast, often used as a retreat.

villager.d: A person who lives in, or comes from, a village.

vinegar.d: A sour liquid formed by the fermentation of alcohol used as a condiment or preservative; a dilute solution of acetic acid.

virtual reality.d: A computer technology that simulates a real or imagined environment so that the user can interact with it as if physically present.

virtually.e: With our medicare supplemental insurance plan, there are virtually no claim forms to fill out. (Advertisement)

visibly.e: He was visibly upset while reading the news live on air about the school shooting.

vital.d: Relating to, or characteristic of life.
vital.e: vital energies; vital functions; vital actions

vitamin.d: Any of a specific group of organic compounds essential in small quantities for healthy human growth, metabolism, development, and body function; found in minute amounts in plant and animal foods or sometimes produced synthetically; deficiencies of specific vitamins produce specific disorders.

vocalist.d: A singer; a person who likes to sing.

vomit.d: The regurgitated former contents of a stomach; vomitus.

wage.d: (often in plural) An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
wage.e: Before her promotion, her wages were 20% less.

waist.d: The part of the body between the pelvis and the stomach.

weed.d: Any plant regarded as unwanted at the place where, and at the time when it is growing.
weed.e: If it isn't in a straight line or marked with a label, it's a weed.

wheat.d: Any of several cereal grains, of the genus Triticum, that yields flour as used in bakery.

winding.d: To blow air through a wind instrument or horn to make a sound.
winding.e: The boxer was winded during round two.

withdraw.d: To pull (something) back, aside, or away.

worn out.d: To cause (something) to become damaged, useless, or ineffective through continued use, especially hard, heavy, or careless use.
worn out.e: That old tractor is worn out.

yacht.d: A slick and light ship for making pleasure trips or racing on water, having sails but often motor-powered. At times used as a residence offshore on a dock.
yacht.e: Would you like to go sailing on my uncle’s yacht?

yawn.d: To open the mouth widely and take a long, rather deep breath, often because one is tired or bored, and sometimes accompanied by pandiculation.
yawn.e: The slideshow we sat through was such a yawn. I was glad when it finished.

yearn.d: To long, have a strong desire (for something).
yearn.e: All I yearn for is a simple life.

yield.d: To pay, give in payment; repay, recompense; reward; requite.

zebra.d: Any of three species of genus Equus: E. grevyi, E. quagga, or E. zebra, all with black and white stripes and native to Africa.

zip.d: The high-pitched sound of a small object moving rapidly through air.

zoom.d: A humming noise from something moving very fast.
